chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the compensation for hunted game: may he eat some of its meat? He said: He may eat from his sacrifice, and he gives the compensation in charity.

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّتِهِ: his sacrificial animal from which he may eat
key_terms.الصَّيْدِ: game animals hunted, the subject of the compensation ruling
key_terms.فِدَاءِ: compensation or expiatory offering due for hunted game
key_terms.لَحْمِهِ: its meat, referring to the meat of the offering
key_terms.يَأْكُلُ: he may eat, indicating permissibility in this legal context
key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقُ: he gives in charity, indicating transfer to the needy

ai.seo_question: Can a person eat from the compensation sacrifice for hunted game in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the compensation connected to hunted game, distinguishing between what may be eaten and what must be given away. The Imam عليه السلام states that one may eat from his sacrificial offering, while the fidāʾ itself is to be given in charity.
